messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: " + "reserved-pool" + ":beta-corp high p99 latency + rising 5xx on tenant gateway -- PD-38591
sre-oncall-1: acked in PD; I'm on it. Anyone with quick visibility on reserved pool HPA and KV metrics? :mag_right:
pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by sre-oncall-1 via PagerDuty UI
devops-priya: grabbing dashboards now -> https://graf.redwood.internal/d/reserved/beta-corp?from=now-2h
runtime-jason: CPU for beta pool nodes pegged ~97-100%. KV-cache churn high, evictions spiking. seeing many long-context requests (~>6k tokens) from same API key
sre-oncall-1: is it multi-tenant effect or isolated?
runtime-jason: isolated to beta-corp reserved pool nodes only, other tenants green
devops-priya: logs sample for beta-corp (redacted):
```
2026-03-11T21:44:12Z beta-gateway WARN req_time_ms=1530 model=gpt-x context_tokens=6180 api_key=beta_*** req_id=abc123
2026-03-11T21:44:13Z reserved-worker ERROR kvcache_eviction=true alloc_retry=2
```
ops-handoff-bot: escalation scheduled in 7m if not claimed by L2
sre-l2-raja: joining. checking HPA + reserved-provisioner: `kubectl -n reserved get hpa beta-corp-reserved -o yaml`
sre-oncall-1: mitigation options: (A) spin extra reserved node(s) from warm pool (B) apply short-term gateway throttle for very large contexts (C) route to quantized variant gpt-x-q8 (D) enable sticky KV cache mode
devops-priya: we have one warm node in standby, can attach in ~90s. starting attach now
runtime-jason: enabling sticky cache might reduce eviction churn: `rtctl cache mode beta-corp sticky` (applies to runtime group)
sre-l2-raja: pushed gateway rule to cap requests with context>5000 to 3 rps per key. rule snippet:
```
# temporary rule
if request.context_len > 5000 and request.per_key_rate > 3:
  respond 429, "beta-corp temporary large-context rate limit"
```
devops-priya: warm node attach logs: node-standby-7 -> attaching (progress 60%)
pagerduty: PD escalation -> notifying SRE Lead (no ack)
sre-oncall-1: acked escalation in PD. Raja, also flip routing fallback to q8 for beta-corp?
sre-l2-raja: applied router change: `routerctl set-fallback --tenant beta-corp --model gpt-x-q8` 
runtime-jason: sticky cache on -> eviction rate down ~65% in last minute
devops-priya: node-standby-7 attached to reserved pool; capacity +1 -> throughput +17%
sre-oncall-1: p99 dropped from ~2.4s -> ~1.0s after throttle + cache + node. 5xx rate dropped from ~1.2% -> 0.3%
beta-corp-monitoring-bot: Auto-alert cleared for beta-corp reserved-pool (throughput/latency normalized)
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident auto-resolved by monitoring bot
sre-oncall-1: marking incident mitigated. Actions recorded: attached standby node, enabled sticky KV cache, temporary gateway large-context throttle, routing fallback to quantized model. Adding notes to incident ticket PD-38591
devops-priya: quick post-action note: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/beta-burst-2026 (runbook stub)
sre-l2-raja: I'll take ownership for RCA. initial hypothesis: sudden client-side batch of very long-context scoring requests circumventing client quotas, causing KV churn + CPU saturation. I'll correlate request IDs with customer deploys
runtime-jason: uploading KV/heap graphs to thread for postmortem: https://graf.redwood.internal/d/reserved/kv-evict?panelId=7
sre-oncall-1: handoff to Raja for root-cause and postmortem, my shift ends in ~30m. Page me if regressions occur
ops-handoff-bot: handoff log: from=sre-oncall-1 to=sre-l2-raja at=2026-03-11T22:30:00Z
sre-l2-raja: acknowledged. next steps: (1) coordinate with Beta-Corp SE to pause batch jobs (2) propose stricter gateway per-key quotas for long-context (3) propose reserved short-burst autoscale policy in Dedicated config
beta-corp-support: thanks team. we've paused client-side eval and rolling back a recent release; will follow up in 10m with results
sre-l2-raja: leaving thread open for updates and will file a postmortem ticket (PM-2026-453) with timeline and remediation items
sre-oncall-1: good work everyone :thumbsup:
pagerduty: Incident closed by sre-oncall-1
